title: big update for my idle rpg just dropped, would love some honest feedback
author: TalesofEternitydev
selftext:
hey all, I've been working on a pixel art idle rpg called Tales of Eternity (plays in your browser, has online multiplayer) and I just pushed the biggest update its ever had



quick backstory, I had people playtest it a while back and the feedback was basically "the start is confusing and I quit". which stung but yeah they were right lol. so most of this update is me trying to fix that



stuff thats new:



\- theres an actual story intro now. you play through a past life, lose a fight you cant win, then make your character and start over

\- the guide shows you what to tap and draws a little sparkle trail to where youre going instead of dumping text on you

\- redid the look of every creature and boss, pets too

\- every skill (woodcutting, mining, fishing, cooking etc) has stuff to earn now, outfits, a pet, trophies, titles

\- every skill card has its own animation, meteor actually falls from the sky now instead of your guy just running up and swinging

\- hidden shards to find in trees and rocks, treasure maps, and a golden goblin that runs away when it sees you

\- keyboard + controller support, new sounds, loads faster

\- a whole pile of bug fixes from the last playtest



if you try it I'd really like to know where you got stuck or bored or just closed the tab. be mean if you have to, the mean feedback last time was the most useful honestly



made a quick form for it, mostly multiple choice and you can skip anything, no sign in



game: [https://im-eternal.itch.io/tales-of-eternity](https://im-eternal.itch.io/tales-of-eternity)



form: [https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSckoBrCcoHiV9wyFRdGgd-NO-yurommEPcw2kB7bbE-vUXlfA/viewform](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSckoBrCcoHiV9wyFRdGgd-NO-yurommEPcw2kB7bbE-vUXlfA/viewform)



thanks for reading, and thanks to everyone who already sent stuff in, I do read all of it

comments.author: OneManGameStudio76
comments.body:
Good call on the sparkle trail instead of text dumps. I played through about 15 min of similar idle games where the UI is just walls of numbers, so seeing that visual cue actually helps me understand what to tap next without stopping the flow.



The skill animations look solid, especially the meteor one. It makes waiting for a cooldown feel more like an event than just staring at a timer. Did you find it hard to keep the idle pacing while adding all these new interactions? Sometimes adding too many things to click can make the game feel less "idle" and more like micro-managing.



I'll check out the form for feedback on the intro confusion.

replies.author: TalesofEternitydev
replies.body: Thanks on the feedback!  I'm honestly aiming more towards a pokemon like combat system, and then MMO features like the Skilling and gear crafting and such and then maybe mix in some idle features as side content.
